newsitem.title: USA: Florida home resales drop 6 percent in May.
newsitem.headline: Florida home resales drop 6 percent in May.

text.p: Florida sales of existing single-family homes in May surpassed April levels but fell short of the benchmark heights set in May of last year, the Florida Association of Realtors said Wednesday.
The association said 12,189 homes changed hands in May, an 8 percent increase from April but a 6 percent decrease compared to May 1996.
The slowdown is explained in part by extremely strong sales last year, when May resales jumped 10 percent as buyers rushed to close deals amid slowly rising interest rates.
The average rate for a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage a year ago was 8.07 percent, compared to 7.94 percent in May 1997.
The median resale price for homes rose 5 percent from year-ago levels to $96,200.

Florida's highest home-resale activity in the Lakeland-Winter Haven area southwest of Walt Disney World, which saw a 21 perent increase. The area is home to increasing numbers of tourism industry employees.
The Naples area saw a 19 percent increase in sales and a 21 percent increase in the median price as the closing on several luxury homes drove up the median.

The area in northern Collier County is benefitting from sales to employees of Florida Gulf Coast University, which opens this fall. The resort area is also enjoying a resurgence of vacation homeownership among South Americans, and British and German families.
Other urban areas and their changes in May home resales, compared with May of last year, were:
Panama City, up 18 percent; Melbourne-Titusville, up 14 percent; Fort Pierce-Port St. Lucie, up 8 percent; Ocala, up 5 percent; Daytona Beach and Jacksonville, both up 2 percent.

Punta Gorda, down 38 percent; Tallahassee, down 25 percent; Fort Lauderdale, down 19 percent; West Palm Beach-Boca Raton, down 16 percent; Sarasota-Bradenton, down 14 percent; Miami, down 13 percent; Fort Walton Beach, down 9 percent; Fort Myers-Cape Coral, down 7 percent; Pensacola, down 5 percent; Tampa-St. Petersburg, down 4 percent; Gainesville, down 3 percent; and Orlando, down 2 percent.
